page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network interfaces that deliver a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25% tier. The processor's extended instructions test also registers in the top 25%, supported by hardware-level AVX and AVX-512 capabilities. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is highly efficient at 209.21 GB/sec, placing it in the upper performance tier. However, single-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, remain in the average tier. LLM text generation speeds are weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both 135M and 7B models, indicating a clear tradeoff when executing real-time generative AI workloads without GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge offers high compute density for parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a cost-effective choice for CPU-bound tasks where paying for excess memory would be inefficient. Strong performance in database operations and multi-threaded processing makes this instance well-suited for high-throughput database servers, multi-threaded compilation, batch processing, and static web serving.
